title: Universal_psychometrics
summary:
Universal psychometrics encompasses psychometric instruments that could measure the psychological properties of any intelligent agent. Up until the early 21st century, psychometrics relied heavily on psychological tests that require the subject to cooperate and answer questions, the most famous example being an intelligence test. Such methods are only applicable to the measurement of human psychological properties.

Some researchers have proposed the idea of universal psychometrics, suggesting the development of testing methods that allow for the measurement of non-human entities' psychological properties. For example, it has been suggested that the Turing test is a form of universal psychometrics. This test involves having testers attempt to distinguish a human from a machine by interacting with both.

The concept was formalized by Hernandez-Orallo and colleagues, who introduced Universal Psychometrics as the analysis and development of measurement techniques and tools for the evaluation of cognitive abilities of subjects in the machine kingdom. The notion of universal psychometrics was proposed as a subject of study, and eventually a discipline, that would focus on the measurement of any interactive cognitive system. The evaluation of abilities, traits, and learning evolution of machines has been mostly unrelated to the case of humans and non-human animals, with specific approaches in the area of artificial intelligence.

A related field is Psychometric AI (PAI), which is devoted to building information-processing entities capable of at least solid performance on all established, validated tests of intelligence and mental ability. More recently, researchers have applied psychometric tools to large language models. Psychometric inventories can be used as diagnostic tools that provide a window into the psychological characteristics of LLMs, which can exhibit or mimic the very same psychological characteristics typically studied in humans, due to being trained on vast corpora of human-written text.
